data.narrative:
Asimov is a Series B biotech company that has raised $209M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of eight private companies and three public comparables in Biotech & Health, including Series B/C-stage firms like Eikon Therapeutics ($539M), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), and New Limit ($3.1B), alongside public peers RXRX, TEM, and ONT.L.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $397M. Peer-median anchoring across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $3.5B implied value, with the peer set ranging from $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue for the target.

These two methods support a triangulated range of $338M (low) to $4.0B (high), with a median of $1.9B. The wide range reflects meaningful dispersion in comparable valuations and stage-specific uncertainty. Stage-progression yields a floor estimate; peer-median anchoring is pulled upward by the inclusion of later-stage Series C companies with established momentum. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, clinical or technical validation progress not captured in public filings, and the timing and structure of the next funding round.
